mainTopic: Who holds that a minor's חליצה is valid (רבי יוסי, proven by the story of רבי ישמעאל and אבדן), the age a קטנה may do חליצה, the three judges required, and the prison חליצה before רבי עקיבא
overview: The גמרא brings רב's teaching that the משנה's rulings on חליצה done by a minor boy or a minor girl follow רבי מאיר. רבי מאיר says the Torah's word 'איש' means the man must be an adult, and the woman is compared to him. The חכמים say only the man must be an adult, and the woman may be a גדולה or a קטנה. The גמרא identifies these חכמים as רבי יוסי and proves it with a long story about רבי ישמעאל בר רבי יוסי in רבי's study hall. The story includes his clash with רבי's attendant אבדן. At the end, רבי ישמעאל quotes his father in the חכמים's exact words, and אבדן is punished for insulting him. The גמרא then discusses how young a קטנה may be: רבי אמי says a little child, and רבא says the age of vows. The הלכה is that she needs שתי שערות. רב נחמן's two rulings together set exactly three judges for חליצה. Finally, the גמרא explains the prison חליצה that רבי עקיבא accepted: witnesses watched from outside, and both the חליצה and the ruling took place in prison.

steps.title: רב says the ruling on a minor boy's חליצה is רבי מאיר's view
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה in the name of רב says the משנה's ruling about חליצה with a boy who is a קטן follows רבי מאיר. The חכמים say that kind of חליצה counts for nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: This is רבי מאיר's opinion. But the חכמים say a minor boy's חליצה is nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב tells us that the משנה's ruling about a minor boy's חליצה is only one side of an argument, the side of רבי מאיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה called this חליצה 'פסולה', meaning invalid but still with some effect. רב says that view is רבי מאיר's. The חכמים go further and say it has no effect at all, as if no חליצה was done.

keyTerms.meaning: The ceremony of removing the shoe, which frees a widow from יבום
A boy who is not yet an adult (under 13)
Anything; with אֵין it means 'nothing at all'
The Sages, the majority opinion against a single named תנא

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
This is the statement of Rabbi Meir,
phrases.notes: 'This' points back to the משנה, which said a חליצה done with a minor boy is 'invalid'.

phrases.english: but the Rabbis say:
The ḥalitza of a male minor is nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב: זוֹ דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attributes the preceding משנה's ruling on a minor boy's חליצה to רבי מאיר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's view that a minor boy's חליצה is 'invalid' but still has some effect belongs to רבי מאיר. The חכמים hold it has no effect at all.

steps.title: A minor girl's חליצה: רב attributes it to רבי מאיר and gives his reason
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's case of a girl who is a קטנה doing חליצה, רב again says it follows רבי מאיר. His reason is that the Torah writes 'man' and the woman is compared to the man, so she must also be an adult.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If a minor girl did חליצה, etc.' רב יהודה said in the name of רב: This is רבי מאיר's view. He said that 'man' is written in the Torah section, and we compare the woman to the man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה about a minor girl. רב says this ruling also belongs to רבי מאיר and explains his source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah section on חליצה calls the brother 'האיש', which means an adult man. רבי מאיר uses a הקש, a comparison, to treat the woman like the man. So a girl who is a קטנה cannot do a fully valid חליצה and must do it again when she grows up.

keyTerms.meaning: A girl who is not yet an adult (under 12)
A section of the Torah, here the section about יבום and חליצה
We compare one thing to another (a הֶקֵּשׁ), so the same rules apply to both

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. Step 1 was about a minor BOY (קטן). This step is about a minor GIRL (קטנה).

phrases.english: If a female minor performed ḥalitza, etc.
phrases.notes: Quoting the משנה, which says she must do חליצה again once she is grown.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
This is the statement of Rabbi Meir, who said:
"Man" is written in the portion,
phrases.notes: דברים 25:7

phrases.english: and we compare a woman to a man.

steps.triggerLanguage: קְטַנָּה שֶׁחָלְצָה וְכוּ׳. אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next case in the משנה and gives the same kind of attribution, this time with a source
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A minor girl's חליצה needs to be repeated as an adult according to רבי מאיר, because the woman is compared to the 'איש' in the פסוק.

steps.title: The חכמים: only the man must be an adult, the woman can be any age
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים agree that 'man' is written, but they say that only tells us the man must be an adult. The woman can be either a גדולה or a קטנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the חכמים say: 'Man' is written in the section. A woman can be either an adult or a minor.
steps.whatsHappening: This finishes רב's statement by giving the other side, the view of the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים do not compare the woman to the man. The word 'איש' only limits the man. Since the Torah does not call the woman 'אשה' here, there is no age requirement for her, and a קטנה's חליצה is valid.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר: 'איש' plus the הקש means both sides must be adults. חכמים: only the man must be an adult, and the woman can be a קטנה.

phrases.english: But the Rabbis say:
"Man" is written in the portion.
A woman — whether an adult or a minor.
phrases.notes: Only the man is called 'man' in the פסוק, so the age rule stops with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רבי מאיר within the same statement of רב
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, the word 'איש' requires only the man to be an adult. A woman's חליצה is valid whether she is a גדולה or a קטנה.

steps.title: Who are these חכמים?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which תנא is behind the anonymous 'חכמים' who argue with רבי מאיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Who are the חכמים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question to find out who the unnamed חכמים are. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is being attacked here. The גמרא wants to put a specific name on the view that a minor girl's חליצה is valid.

phrases.english: Who are the Rabbis?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the identity of the חכמים mentioned in Step 3
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which specific תנא holds that a woman's חליצה is valid even when she is a minor?

steps.title: It is רבי יוסי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the חכמים here are רבי יוסי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is רבי יוסי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the view of the חכמים is really the view of רבי יוסי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא names the opinion here and will back it up with a story in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: It is; used to identify whose opinion something is

phrases.english: It is Rabbi Yosei.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The חכמים who allow a minor girl's חליצה are רבי יוסי.

steps.title: A story begins: רבי חייא and רבי שמעון discuss where to look when praying
steps.stepSummary: To show that the חכמים are רבי יוסי, the גמרא opens a story. רבי חייא and רבי שמעון בר רבי were sitting together, and one of them said that a person praying should look downward, based on a פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי חייא and רבי שמעון בר רבי were sitting. One of them began and said: One who prays should put his eyes downward, as it says: 'And My eyes and My heart shall be there all the days.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story that will prove רבי יוסי is the תנא behind the חכמים. This step only sets up the story. The proof comes in step 18, where רבי יוסי's son quotes his father using the חכמים's exact words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story opens with a discussion about תפילה that seems unrelated. One rabbi says to look down when praying, because the פסוק says ה׳'s 'eyes and heart' are 'there', in the בית המקדש. The link to רבי יוסי and חליצה will come as the story goes on.

keyTerms.meaning: He opened, meaning he began speaking

steps.confusionAlert: The discussion about תפילה is not the point of this proof. It is the opening of a longer story that will later connect to רבי יוסי.

phrases.aramaic: דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר רַבִּי
phrases.english: For Rabbi Ḥiyya and Rabbi Shimon son of Rabbi
phrases.notes: The 'For' tells you this story is how we know it's רבי יוסי. 'רבי' here means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: were sitting.
One of them began and said:
One who prays must direct his eyes downward,
as it is stated:
"And My eyes and My heart shall be there all the days."
phrases.notes: מלכים א 9:3

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בַּר רַבִּי הֲווֹ יָתְבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the story that supports the answer of Step 5
steps.raayaObject: The identification of the חכמים as רבי יוסי
steps.raayaSupportSource: A story about רבי חייא and רבי שמעון בר רבי, which begins with a discussion about where to look during תפילה

steps.title: The second opinion: eyes should look upward
steps.stepSummary: The other sage in the story says a person praying should look upward, based on a פסוק in איכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one said: his eyes should face upward, because the פסוק says, 'Let us lift up our hearts with our hands.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. The second sage gives the opposite view: during תפלה your eyes should look up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each sage now has a פסוק. One פסוק points the eyes down, and this one points the heart and hands up toward heaven. That sets up a clash that someone will need to resolve.

phrases.english: And one said: his eyes should be upward,
as it says: 'Let us lift our hearts with our hands.'
phrases.notes: איכה 3:41

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to step 6 inside the same story.
steps.raayaObject: That the anonymous חכמים are רבי יוסי
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רבי חייא and רבי שמעון בר רבי, which leads to a statement of רבי יוסי

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל בר רבי יוסי arrives and asks what they are discussing
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בר רבי יוסי joins them and asks what they are learning. They tell him: תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile, רבי ישמעאל בר רבי יוסי came over to them. He asked them, 'What are you busy with?' They answered, 'With תפלה.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new person enters the story. This is a setup line: his question prepares the way for him to settle their argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל is the son of רבי יוסי. His arrival matters because he will report his father's view, and the גמרא is trying to show what רבי יוסי holds.

keyTerms.meaning: you are busy with, dealing with

phrases.english: In the meantime, there came
Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei, over to them.
He said to them: What are you dealing with?
They said to him: With prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַדְּהָכִי אֲתָא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings in the son of רבי יוסי to respond to the argument in steps 6 and 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What topic the two sages are discussing

steps.title: רבי יוסי's view: eyes down, heart up
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל quotes his father, רבי יוסי: a person praying should look down and direct his heart up, so that both פסוקים are kept.
steps.simpleTranslation: He told them, 'This is what my father said: a person who prays must put his eyes downward and his heart upward, so that both of these פסוקים are kept.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל settles the argument by quoting his father, רבי יוסי. You don't have to choose one פסוק, because each one refers to a different part of you.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of choosing a side, רבי יוסי splits the two פסוקים: the eyes follow the first one and the heart follows the second. This teaching about תפילה is not yet the proof about חליצה. That comes later in the story, when רבי ישמעאל quotes his father's ruling on a קטנה (step 18).
steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי: during תפלה, the eyes look down and the heart is directed up, which fulfills both פסוקים.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known teaching about how to stand during תפלה. It also brings רבי יוסי's voice into the story, which the גמרא needs for its proof.

phrases.english: He said to them: Thus said my father:
phrases.notes: His father is רבי יוסי, the Tanna the גמרא is trying to identify.

phrases.english: One who prays needs to put
his eyes downward and his heart upward,
so that both of these verses are fulfilled.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the disagreement from steps 6 and 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Keep both פסוקים: the eyes look down and the heart is directed up.

steps.title: רבי enters and רבי ישמעאל steps over people to reach his seat
steps.stepSummary: רבי comes into the בית מדרש. Lighter people quickly reach their seats, but the heavy רבי ישמעאל has to step over people as he walks.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile, רבי came to the study hall. The people who were light on their feet sat down in their places. רבי ישמעאל בר רבי יוסי, because he was heavy, was stepping over people as he went.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves to a new scene. This sets up the clash that follows, because רבי ישמעאל ends up stepping over the people seated on the floor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is ruled here. The point is the situation: everyone else is already seated, so רבי ישמעאל has to step over them. That looks disrespectful and leads straight to the challenge in the next step.

phrases.english: In the meantime, Rabbi came to the study hall.
phrases.notes: 'רבי' alone means רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: Those who were light on their feet
sat down in their places.
Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei,
because of his heaviness,
was stepping along as he went.
phrases.notes: Everyone was already sitting on the floor, so he had to step over them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves the story into רבי's study hall.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Narrative only: רבי ישמעאל steps over seated people because he is heavy.

steps.title: אבדן objects to someone stepping over a holy nation
steps.stepSummary: אבדן calls out, 'Who is stepping over the heads of a holy people?' רבי ישמעאל says who he is and that he came to learn from רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבדן said to him, 'Who is this stepping over the heads of a holy people?' He answered, 'I am ישמעאל בר רבי יוסי, and I came to learn Torah from רבי.'
steps.whatsHappening: אבדן objects to what he sees as disrespect. רבי ישמעאל defends himself by saying who he is and why he came.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is about behavior: stepping over people is an insult to them. רבי ישמעאל answers that his purpose is learning Torah, which sets up אבדן's sharper question in the next step.

phrases.english: Abdon said to him:
Who is this who is stepping
over the heads of a holy people!

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנִי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי
phrases.english: He said to him: I am Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei
who came to learn Torah from Rabbi.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי הוּא זֶה שֶׁמְּפַסֵּעַ עַל רָאשֵׁי עַם קָדוֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reacts to רבי ישמעאל stepping over people in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's behavior of stepping over seated people
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Stepping over a holy people's heads is disrespectful.

steps.title: Are you worthy to learn from רבי?
steps.stepSummary: אבדן pushes further and asks if רבי ישמעאל is even fit to learn from רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבדן said to him, 'And are you worthy to learn Torah from רבי?'
steps.whatsHappening: אבדן turns רבי ישמעאל's own answer against him. He suggests that someone who acts this way is not fit to learn from so great a teacher.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge moves from the action itself to the person doing it. The underlying claim is that a student must be worthy of his teacher.

phrases.english: He said to him: And are you worthy
to learn Torah from Rabbi?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי אַתָּה הָגוּן לִלְמוֹד תּוֹרָה מֵרַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns רבי ישמעאל's explanation in step 11 against him.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's claim that he came to learn from רבי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A student must be worthy of his teacher, and this behavior shows he is not.

steps.title: Was משה worthy to learn from ה׳?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל replies that משה רבינו was not truly 'worthy' of learning from ה׳ either, yet he learned.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him, 'And was משה worthy to learn Torah from the mouth of the Almighty?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל answers with a question of his own: no student is ever fully worthy of his teacher, and that has never stopped anyone from learning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He rejects the idea behind the attack, that a student must be equal to his teacher. משה learned from ה׳ even though no one could be worthy of that.

keyTerms.meaning: from the mouth of the Almighty

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְכִי מֹשֶׁה הָיָה הָגוּן
phrases.english: He said to him: And was Moses worthy
to learn Torah from the mouth of the Almighty?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the premise by comparison to משה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A student must be as worthy as his teacher.
steps.terutzMaskana: A student does not have to equal his teacher in order to learn from him.

steps.title: Are you משה?
steps.stepSummary: אבדן attacks the comparison: you are not משה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him, 'And are you משה?'
steps.whatsHappening: אבדן rejects the comparison. He says רבי ישמעאל cannot compare himself to משה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The attack is on the analogy itself. משה was special, so what applied to him may not apply to an ordinary student.

phrases.english: He said to him: And are you Moses?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the comparison made in step 13.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: משה was unique, so the comparison does not work.

steps.title: Is your teacher God?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל shoots back: and is your teacher God?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him, 'And is your teacher God?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל flips the objection. If I am not משה, then רבי is not God either, so the gap between me and רבי is far smaller.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison holds because both sides of it shrink together. If the student is lesser than משה, the teacher is much lesser than ה׳, so it is even more acceptable for him to learn.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְכִי רַבְּךָ אֱלֹהִים הוּא?
phrases.english: He said to him: And is your teacher God?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the comparison from the attack in step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the student is not משה, the comparison fails.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since the teacher is not God either, the comparison still works.

steps.title: רב יוסף: רבי was paid back for his silence
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף comments that רבי received his punishment here, because רבי ישמעאל said 'your teacher' and not 'my teacher.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: רבי got his payback here, because רבי ישמעאל said to אבדן 'your teacher' and not 'my teacher.'
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא steps in to comment on the story. רב יוסף points out that the wording 'your teacher' was a measure-for-measure punishment for רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי stayed silent while his student insulted רבי ישמעאל. So רבי ישמעאל's choice of words, 'your teacher', hinted that he did not accept רבי as his own teacher.

keyTerms.meaning: took his payback, received his punishment
my teacher (also the name for רבי יהודה הנשיא)

steps.confusionAlert: In the last line, 'רבי' is not the name רבי יהודה הנשיא. It is the plain word 'my teacher', contrasted with 'your teacher.'

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
Rabbi received his payback
phrases.notes: This was for staying quiet while his student shamed רבי ישמעאל.

phrases.english: in that he said to him 'your teacher' and not 'my teacher.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף: שַׁקְלֵיהּ רַבִּי לְמַטְרַפְסֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the wording רבי ישמעאל used in step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Calling רבי 'your teacher' rather than 'my teacher' was רבי's measure-for-measure punishment for staying silent.

steps.title: A young יבמה comes, and רבי sends אבדן to check her
steps.stepSummary: A יבמה comes before רבי, and רבי sends אבדן out to check her.
steps.simpleTranslation: Meanwhile a יבמה came before רבי. רבי told אבדן: Go out and check her.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves to a new event: a young יבמה arrives. This sets up the next move, where רבי ישמעאל will share a ruling that makes the check unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question is whether she is old enough for her חליצה to count, so רבי sends אבדן to examine her. This shows that רבי was acting as if she had to be an adult for her חליצה to count; the open question was her age, until he hears רבי יוסי's ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A widow whose husband died without children, waiting for יבום or חליצה

phrases.english: In the meantime, a yevama came before Rabbi.
Rabbi said to Abdon:
Go out and check her.
phrases.notes: He means: check whether she is grown up enough for her חליצה to count.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story of רבי, רבי ישמעאל and אבדן with a new event.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי wants the girl checked for maturity before accepting her חליצה.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל quotes his father: a minor girl may do חליצה
steps.stepSummary: After אבדן leaves, רבי ישמעאל quotes רבי יוסי: the פסוק says 'man', so only the man must be an adult, while the woman may be adult or minor.
steps.simpleTranslation: After אבדן went out, רבי ישמעאל said to רבי: My father said this: 'Man' is written in the passage, but a woman may be either an adult or a minor.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל gives a ruling from his father, רבי יוסי, that answers the question about the young יבמה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the payoff of the whole story. רבי יוסי's words, 'איש כתוב בפרשה, אבל אשה בין גדולה בין קטנה', match the חכמים in step 3 word for word. That proves the answer in step 5: the חכמים are רבי יוסי. As for the young יבמה, only the man must be an adult, so the check is not needed.

keyTerms.meaning: The Torah passage, here the section about חליצה

steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling of רבי יוסי is the source the rest of the daf builds on when it asks what age a קטנה must be.

phrases.english: After he went out,
Rabbi Yishmael said to him:
So said my father:
phrases.notes: His father is רבי יוסי.

phrases.english: "Man" is written in the passage,
phrases.notes: דברים 25:7

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אִשָּׁה — בֵּין גְּדוֹלָה בֵּין קְטַנָּה.
phrases.english: but a woman may be either an adult or a minor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the ruling that settles the question raised by sending אבדן to check. Its wording matches the חכמים in step 3, which completes the proof that the חכמים are רבי יוסי (step 5).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only the man doing חליצה must be an adult; the woman may be a minor.

steps.title: רבי accepts the ruling and calls אבדן back
steps.stepSummary: רבי tells אבדן to come back, because the Elder, רבי יוסי, has already ruled.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said to אבדן: Come back. You are not needed, because the Elder has already ruled.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי accepts רבי יוסי's ruling right away and calls off the check.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי treats the ruling of רבי יוסי as settled and calls him 'the Elder' with respect. This leaves אבדן with no job to do, which sets up the next scene.

phrases.english: He said to him: Come back,
phrases.notes: רבי is calling אבדן back.

phrases.english: you are not needed,
the Elder has already ruled.
phrases.notes: The Elder is רבי יוסי, whose ruling was just quoted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי accepts the ruling given in the previous step.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Following רבי יוסי, the girl does not need to be checked.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל rebukes אבדן for stepping over people
steps.stepSummary: As אבדן steps over the seated students, רבי ישמעאל says that only someone the people need may step over them.
steps.simpleTranslation: אבדן was stepping over people as he came back. רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי said to him: Someone the holy people need may step over the heads of the holy people. But how can someone the holy people do not need step over their heads?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל attacks אבדן's behavior with a sharp rhetorical question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stepping over seated people can be allowed when someone is on an errand the people need. Now that his errand was cancelled, אבדן had no such reason, so his stepping over them was disrespectful.

phrases.english: Abdon was stepping over people and coming back.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei said to him:
One whom the holy people needs
may step over the heads of the holy people.

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁאֵין צָרִיךְ לוֹ עַם קָדוֹשׁ,
phrases.english: One whom the holy people does not need,

phrases.aramaic: הֵיאַךְ יְפַסֵּעַ עַל רָאשֵׁי עַם קָדוֹשׁ?
phrases.english: how may he step over the heads of the holy people?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the cancelled errand: now אבדן has no reason to step over people.
steps.kashyaTarget: אבדן's stepping over the seated students
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Stepping over people is allowed only for someone the people need; אבדן's task was cancelled, so he is no longer needed.

steps.title: רבי tells אבדן to stay where he is
steps.stepSummary: רבי tells אבדן to stand in his place, agreeing that he should not keep stepping over people.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי said to אבדן: Stand in your place!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי backs up רבי ישמעאל's rebuke and stops אבדן from going any further.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By telling אבדן to stay put, רבי shows that רבי ישמעאל's complaint is correct. The scene now closes before the ברייתא reports what happened to אבדן.

phrases.english: Rabbi said to Abdon:
Stand in your place!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי agrees with רבי ישמעאל's rebuke.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבדן must stop and stay where he is.

steps.title: A ברייתא tells of אבדן's punishments
steps.stepSummary: At that moment אבדן was struck with צרעת, two of his sons drowned, and his two daughters-in-law did מיאון.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: At that moment אבדן became a מצורע, his two sons drowned, and his two daughters-in-law did מיאון.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא reports the harsh punishments that came upon אבדן right then.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The timing, 'at that moment', links the punishments to how אבדן treated רבי ישמעאל. These are three separate disasters: illness, the death of his sons, and his daughters-in-law ending their marriages through מיאון.

keyTerms.meaning: Became a מצורע, struck with צרעת
Did מיאון, refused and undid the marriage

phrases.english: It was taught: At that moment
Abdon was struck with tzara'at,
and his two sons drowned,
and his two daughters-in-law refused.
phrases.notes: מיאון is a refusal that undoes a marriage made while the girl was still a minor.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports what happened to אבדן after the rebuke.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אבדן was punished at once with צרעת, the death of his sons, and the מיאון of his daughters-in-law.

steps.title: רב נחמן בר יצחק: good that אבדן was shamed in this world
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק blesses ה׳ for shaming אבדן in this world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: Blessed is the Merciful One, Who shamed אבדן in this world.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק comments on the story and gives a positive way to see אבדן's suffering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He stresses 'in this world'. The point is that being shamed here was a kindness compared to being punished later.
steps.whatToRemember: The story of אבדן ends here: he insulted רבי ישמעאל, was rebuked and punished, and רב נחמן בר יצחק sees the punishment in this world as a kindness.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said:
Blessed is the Merciful One
Who shamed Abdon in this world.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Comments on the punishments described in the ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: It was a mercy that אבדן was shamed in this world.

steps.title: רבי אמי: a minor may do חליצה even as a small child
steps.stepSummary: רבי אמי learns from רבי יוסי's words that a קטנה may do חליצה even at a very young age.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אמי said: From the words of the great man we learn that a minor may do חליצה even when she is a little child.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the הלכה from the story and asks how young the קטנה may be. רבי אמי gives the youngest answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי said 'between an adult and a minor' without giving an age. רבי אמי reads this as broadly as possible, so it includes even a פעוטה, a little child.

keyTerms.meaning: The great man, a title for a leading scholar (here רבי יוסי)
Early childhood, around six or seven

phrases.english: Rabbi Ami said:
From the words of the great man let us learn:
phrases.notes: The great man is רבי יוסי, whose ruling his son quoted.

phrases.english: A minor girl may do chalitza even as a little child.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the story and returns to the הלכה of רבי יוסי from step 18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קטנה may do חליצה even at the age of פעוטות.

steps.title: רבא: only once she reaches the age of vows
steps.stepSummary: רבא says a קטנה may do חליצה only once she reaches עונת נדרים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: She may not do חליצה until she reaches the age of vows.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא disagrees with רבי אמי and sets an older minimum age.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא agrees that a minor can do חליצה, but not a very young child. She must reach עונת נדרים, the age when her understanding is enough for her vows to be examined.

keyTerms.meaning: The age of vows, about eleven

phrases.english: Rava said:
Not until she reaches the age of vows.
phrases.notes: That is about eleven, when a girl's vows are checked to see whether she understands them.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר: עַד שֶׁתַּגִּיעַ לְעוֹנַת נְדָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a different, older age than רבי אמי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קטנה may do חליצה only from עונת נדרים.

steps.title: The halacha: only once she has two hairs
steps.stepSummary: The final הלכה is that she may not do חליצה until she has שתי שערות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה is: not until she has two hairs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling, and it is stricter than both רבי אמי and רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two hairs are the sign of physical maturity. In practice, the girl must be physically mature before her חליצה counts, which brings us back to why רבי first sent אבדן to check her.

keyTerms.meaning: Two hairs, the sign of physical maturity

steps.whatToRemember: רבי אמי says a little child, רבא says the age of vows, but the הלכה is that a girl may do חליצה only once she has שתי שערות.
steps.confusionAlert: Even though רבי יוסי's ruling was praised in the story, the final הלכה does not let a young minor do חליצה. She must show signs of maturity.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule for when a יבמה's חליצה is valid.

phrases.english: And the halacha is:
Not until she has two hairs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides the disagreement between רבי אמי and רבא with a stricter standard.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: A girl may do חליצה only after she has שתי שערות, the sign of physical maturity.

steps.title: רב נחמן rules against the pair who accept two judges
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that the הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון ורבי יוחנן הסנדלר, who accept a חליצה done before two judges.
steps.simpleTranslation: About the משנה's case of חליצה before two judges: רב יוסף בר מניומי said in the name of רב נחמן that the הלכה does not follow that pair of תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה and brings רב נחמן's ruling on it: we do not follow the two תנאים who accept a חליצה before only two judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה, רבי שמעון ורבי יוחנן הסנדלר accept a חליצה done before two judges. רב נחמן says the הלכה does not follow them, so two judges are not enough.

keyTerms.meaning: The ceremony that frees a יבמה from יבום
A pair, here two תנאים who hold the same view
The law does not follow (this opinion)

phrases.english: She performed ḥalitza before two, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: two judges, or three where one turned out unfit. רבי שמעון ורבי יוחנן הסנדלר accept it.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef bar Minyumi said
that Rav Naḥman said:
The halakha does not follow that pair.
phrases.notes: 'That pair' means רבי שמעון ורבי יוחנן הסנדלר.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חליצה before only two valid judges is not accepted. The הלכה does not follow רבי שמעון ורבי יוחנן הסנדלר.

steps.title: Didn't רב נחמן already say this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רב נחמן already said 'חליצה בשלשה', so why repeat himself?
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב נחמן already said this once! רב יוסף בר מניומי said in רב נחמן's name that חליצה needs three judges.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new ruling as unneeded, since רב נחמן already said that חליצה needs three judges.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If חליצה needs three judges, it is obvious that two are not enough. So the ruling against 'that pair' seems to add nothing new.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן חֲדָא זִימְנָא.
phrases.english: But Rav Naḥman already said this one time!
For Rav Yosef bar Minyumi said
that Rav Naḥman said:
Ḥalitza is before three!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן חֲדָא זִימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling in step 27 as a repeat.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב נחמן's ruling 'אין הלכה כאותו הזוג'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His earlier rule 'חליצה בשלשה' already rules out two judges, so the second statement seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Both rulings are needed
steps.stepSummary: Each ruling blocks a mistake the other alone would allow: 'three' alone might mean three only from the start, and 'not that pair' alone might mean five from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are needed. If we only had 'חליצה בשלשה', I would think three is needed only from the start, but after the fact two is fine. So he teaches that the הלכה does not follow that pair. If we only had 'the הלכה does not follow that pair, but the תנא קמא', I would think three works only after the fact, and from the start you need five. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that each of רב נחמן's statements teaches something the other one doesn't.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'חליצה בשלשה' alone could be read as a rule only for the start (לכתחילה), with two still valid after the fact. 'Not that pair' fixes that: two is not valid even after the fact. 'Not that pair' alone could suggest three works only after the fact and five is needed from the start. 'חליצה בשלשה' fixes that: three is fine even from the start.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a wrong first idea)
From the start, the proper way
The first, unnamed תנא of the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: Three judges are both needed and enough for חליצה. Two is not valid even after the fact, and five is not needed even from the start.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two 'I would have thought' ideas. The first wrongly lowers the bar after the fact (two is fine). The second wrongly raises it from the start (five is needed). Each statement of רב נחמן blocks one of them.

phrases.english: Both are needed,
for if only that first one were said,
phrases.notes: The 'first one' is 'חליצה בשלשה' from step 28.

phrases.english: I would have thought:
this applies only from the start,
but after the fact, even two is fine.
So he teaches us:
the halakha does not follow that pair.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַשְׁמוֹעִינַן אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּאוֹתוֹ הַזּוּג,
phrases.english: And if he had only taught us that the halakha does not follow that pair,
but rather the first tanna,
I would have thought: [three works] after the fact,
but from the start one would need five.
phrases.notes: Five is the number רבי יהודה requires in the משנה.

phrases.english: So both are needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: shows that each statement is needed
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only one statement, we could think two judges are enough after the fact, or that five are needed from the start.
steps.terutzMaskana: Together the two rulings set the number at exactly three, both from the start and after the fact.

steps.title: How do we know what happened in private?
steps.stepSummary: About the prison חליצה רבי עקיבא accepted, the גמרא asks how anyone knew what happened between the two of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה tells of a case where they did חליצה, etc. If it was just between him and her, how do we know what happened?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה's story of a private חליצה in prison and asks how רבי עקיבא could accept it with no one there to see it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חליצה done with no one watching seems impossible to confirm. The question asks what the case really was that let רבי עקיבא accept it.

keyTerms.meaning: Between him and her, in private

phrases.english: There was an incident where they did ḥalitza, etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: a couple did חליצה alone in prison, and רבי עקיבא accepted it.

phrases.english: Between him and her,
how do we know [what happened]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next line of the משנה, a new topic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How a private חליצה could be confirmed and accepted.

steps.title: Witnesses watched from outside
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that witnesses saw the חליצה from outside the prison.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in שמואל's name: there were witnesses watching it from outside.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the חליצה was not really unwitnessed, because witnesses saw it from outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Between him and her' means no one else was in the room with them. It does not mean no one saw it. Witnesses outside could see that it was done properly.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
And witnesses were seeing it from outside.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 30.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Witnesses outside saw the חליצה, so it could be confirmed.

steps.title: Where did the חליצה take place?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the חליצה happened outside and only the ruling came to רבי עקיבא in prison, or whether the חליצה itself happened in prison.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked: did the private חליצה happen outside, and the case then came before רבי עקיבא while he was in prison? Or did the private חליצה itself take place in prison?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a question about the משנה's story: which part happened in prison, the חליצה or only the ruling?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'in prison' in the משנה could describe where the חליצה was done. They could also describe only where רבי עקיבא was when he ruled. The question asks which reading is right.

phrases.english: They asked:
Was the incident, where they did ḥalitza between him and her, outside,
phrases.notes: 'Outside' here means somewhere other than the prison.

phrases.aramaic: וּבָא מַעֲשֶׂה לִפְנֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא בְּבֵית הָאֲסוּרִין,
phrases.english: and the case came before Rabbi Akiva in prison,
or perhaps:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁחָלְצוּ בֵּינוֹ לְבֵינָהּ בְּבֵית הָאֲסוּרִין?
phrases.english: the incident of ḥalitza between him and her was in prison?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a further question about the same story in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the חליצה itself, or only the ruling, happened in prison.

steps.title: Both happened in prison
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that the חליצה took place in prison, and the case came to רבי עקיבא in prison too.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in רב's name: the incident happened in prison, and the case came to רבי עקיבא in prison.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: both the חליצה and רבי עקיבא's ruling happened in prison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'in prison' in the משנה cover both parts of the story. The couple did the חליצה in prison, and רבי עקיבא, also in prison, ruled on it.
steps.whatToRemember: In the prison story, the חליצה was done in prison with witnesses watching from outside, and רבי עקיבא ruled on it while he was in prison too.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
The incident happened in prison,
and the case came [to Rabbi Akiva] in prison.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 32.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both the חליצה and the ruling took place in prison.
